players.product: NovaSeq sequencing, BioInsight, and Billion Cell Atlas multi-omics data

quarterly_data.signal: Clinical markets represent approximately 65% of sequencing consumables revenue. CFO: first-half clinical sequencing consumables growth was approximately 17%, with slower growth in the Europe, Middle East and Latin America region; the company raised its clinical growth outlook and now expects mid-teens growth for the year. Research and applied sequencing consumables declined 7% rest of world (9% revenue growth quarter-over-quarter), and management continues to expect mid to high single-digit declines for research and applied consumables in 2026. CEO: oncology leads clinical growth, with MRD starting to drive momentum, while therapy selection is still larger in dollars.
quarterly_data.figure: clinical ~65% of sequencing consumables revenue; first-half clinical growth ~17%; 2026 clinical outlook mid-teens; research and applied consumables declined 7% rest of world

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q3 2026 guidance is rest of world organic revenue growth of approximately 4.5%, reported revenue of $1.14 billion-$1.16 billion, non-GAAP EPS of $1.33-$1.38 and non-GAAP operating margin of approximately 24%. Full-year 2026 rest of world organic growth guidance was raised to greater than 5% from 2%-4%, diluted EPS guidance is $5.30-$5.40 and operating margin guidance of 23.4%-23.6% is maintained; rest of world organic sequencing consumables are expected to grow mid-single digits and sequencing instruments low single digits. CEO: still very committed to delivering high single-digit revenue growth in 2027. CFO: still believes new products will add one to two points of growth next year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $1.14 billion-$1.16 billion; Q3 non-GAAP EPS $1.33-$1.38; FY2026 EPS $5.30-$5.40; FY2026 rest of world organic growth >5%

quarterly_data.signal: Microarrays and other revenue of $105 million was up 21% reported and included SomaLogic revenue, which the CFO said continues to track towards the high end of the deal expectations; on a rest of world organic basis microarrays and other revenue declined 4%. CEO: proteomics momentum is sustained following the close of the SomaLogic acquisition, and the newly branded SomaScan and SomaSeq offerings are generating strong interest.
quarterly_data.figure: microarrays and other revenue $105 million (+21% reported; -4% rest of world organic)

quarterly_data.signal: Illumina launched its whole genome MRD research workflow, which runs on NovaSeq systems and is now in early access with select customers, and this summer launched StrataMap Spatial, its sequencing-based spatial workflow. CEO: interest in StrataMap is higher than planned and TruPath also has momentum. CFO: multi-omics products such as Single Cell and TruPath show up in consumables revenue, while Billion Cell Atlas and related BioInsight revenue show up in services.

CFO: the quarter absorbed higher freight and memory costs; the higher memory cost is in the Q2 results as a run-rate starting point, and the company secured additional inventory and supply of critical components for the next several quarters to de-risk near-term memory price movements, which with tax-payment timing kept operating cash flow of $201 million below the usual trend. CEO: the company is sharing some of the cost increase with customers. CFO: Illumina's instruments do not use GPU architecture. Supply investments allowed the Q2 NovaSeq X placements, with several multi-unit capacity expansion orders from some of the largest clinical customers, including for the start of new clinical trials.

CFO: NovaSeq X placements are still about 70% clinical and 30% research; approximately 78% of clinical volume is now on the X, and clinical volumes are expected to reach 80%-85% conversion by the end of 2026. Over 10 NovaSeq 6000 units were also placed. Sequencing service and other revenue of $154 million was up 14%; the CFO cited traction in the Billion Cell Atlas program resulting in higher data revenue from biopharma customers; instrument growth was driven by NovaSeq X and the MiSeq i100.
quarterly_data.figure: placements ~70% clinical / 30% research; ~78% of clinical volume on NovaSeq X (80%-85% by end of 2026); sequencing service and other revenue $154 million (+14%)
